newsitem.title: ITALY: Hard left seen backing Italy's Prodi after speech.
newsitem.headline: Hard left seen backing Italy's Prodi after speech.

text.p: Senior politicians from Italy's hard left Communist Refoundation party said on Thursday that they expected the party to back Prime Minister Romano Prodi in a confidence vote that will decide the future of his government.

They spoke after Prodi addressed the Senate (upper house) at the start of a confidence test called after Refoundation refused to back him on Wednesday in a separate vote on sending an Italian-led security force to Albania.
"It is a speech that gives us the basis to vote our confidence in him," said Leonardo Caponi, chairman of the Senate industry commission and a senior Refoundation member.
Another Refoundation politician, Enrica Salvati, said she also expected to vote 'yes' but added: "Our leadership will have to decide".

Prodi's centre-left government has a majority in its own right in the Senate but relies for survival on Refoundation in the lower Chamber of Deputies, where a similar confidence vote is scheduled for Saturday. The party is not in government.

Prodi called in his speech on all parties that back him in the confidence vote to support his programme. The remark was a clear reference to Refoundation, which is at odds with the government on key economic issues, including welfare reforms.
